environment.note: headless Chromium with --disable-gpu; frame distributions are diagnostics, not device FPS. localhost with cache disabled is a cold server-speed bound, not a field network measurement. A permanent rAF monitor is part of the sampling path, so no arm can prove zero idle page work; the monitor sets the cadence floor and the counters are attribution only. customPropertyWrites counts CSSStyleDeclaration.setProperty, not direct style.transform assignments. Fetch interception is scoped to the two module URLs, so media Range responses are never paused.

method.frames: one permanent rAF monitor samples deltas; a sampling-only rAF monitor is part of the path, so no arm proves zero idle work

method.interception_scope: Fetch interception patterns are limited to stage.mjs, focus.mjs and arcs.mjs, so media Range responses are never paused

stationary window with the tracer attached; compare with desktop/shipped

traced_window.overhead_pair: traced 37 of 90 frames > 25 ms versus 41 of 90 untraced, p50 16.7 ms both: the tracer is not producing the effect
traced_window.note: Inclusive, potentially overlapping durations; do not sum rows.
traced_window.read: Display::DrawAndSwap is 89 draws totalling 2077 ms on the viz thread (~23 ms per draw, ~40 draws/s in a 2.2 s window); the renderer main thread is 90 BeginMainFrame in 237 ms (~2.6 ms per frame) and 90 ProduceCanvasResource in 56 ms. This is a software-compositor draw cost, not JavaScript and not canvas raster.

notes: Rep 1 of the desktop matrix is the first cold page of the session and reads 33.2 ms stationary p50 with 43 of 86 frames over 25 ms; reps 2 and 3 read 16.7 ms. The arm order is reversed on even reps, so one warmup rep lands on the shipped arm; medians are reported unchanged rather than trimmed.
Two draws in the traced window exceed 40 ms; the per-draw mean is the honest figure, not an FPS claim.
The isolated cost tracks the masked arcs composite plus the per-frame torus transform: no-arcs (34 of 90 second-frames) and no-mask (22 of 90) stay costly, no-transform reaches 0 of 90.

Every isolation arm keeps the per-frame data-stage-state and classList churn because the stage module is unmodified, so removed attribute churn must not be claimed as frame time. It remains a defensible correctness gate.
no-clocks is not a no-JavaScript arm: navigation, media and contact scripts still run. Actual no-JS output is checked by the Ruby page contract and the existing browser gates.
Phone touch displacement varies 335-438 px between arms because it is sampled mid-fling, so phone ink-write counts are confounded by distance and are NOT reported as an ink-rate regression.
No second representation (bake, promotion, cadence change) is justified by these numbers, and nothing here has been measured on real GPU or real device hardware.

Audit of the five pre-existing experiences probes: none of them measures time. experiences.mjs / experiences-focus.mjs / experiences-tree.mjs / experiences-stage.mjs / experiences-type.mjs are correctness and geometry gates with no LCP, resource-timing, rAF or LoAF instrumentation, and their default ports disagree (4001/4012/4022), so a default invocation can silently point at another session's server. This probe is therefore the first timing harness for /experiences, not a replacement for those gates.

Corrected framing of the shipped medians: cold-localhost LCP is 232 ms desktop and 240 ms phone for the shipped arm; the 128-256 ms range quoted elsewhere belongs to abbreviated arms, which is attribution and not a shipped number.

Harness validation recorded: the full default matrix now runs end to end on both devices with every arm-identity assertion green; the earlier partial runs were filtered subsets and are superseded for harness-soundness purposes, not for their numbers.
probe_infra_change: design/probe/cdp.mjs newPage now also returns targetId (additive only) so a probe can close its target instead of leaking a renderer.
confounds: Phone touch displacement is sampled mid-fling and varies 335-438 px between arms, so phone ink-write counts (60 shipped vs 282-298 no-stage) mix distance with rate and are not reported as an ink-rate regression. A displacement-matched gesture is the test that would close this, not a new representation.

The no-arcs arm removes canvas invalidation as well as canvas raster: a no-op drawArcs never clears, so the compositor can reuse the previous canvas tile. It rules out canvas raster as the dominant cost (the traced ProduceCanvasResource is 56 ms per 90 frames) but it does not price invalidation separately.
The no-transform arm swallows transform writes after load, so the torus keeps no transform at all rather than a frozen non-zero one. It is an attribution arm, not a shipped candidate.
Every number is headless Chromium with --disable-gpu on SwiftShader Subzero: a software compositor. Real GPU and real device hardware are unmeasured, and no FPS, INP or field claim follows.

Cold localhost has ~4 ms TTFB and no RTT, so LCP here is bytes-becoming-pixels. The 1.6 Mbps / 150 ms / 4x model from the front page has not been run for /experiences and must not be projected from these numbers.
Stationary drops appear at 1440x900 desktop and not at 390x844 / 4x CPU phone; that is a property of this compositor and viewport, not evidence that the phone is free of the cost.

spike_will_change.decision: REJECTED. No arm reduces the stationary or scroll second-frame count beyond arm-to-arm noise, the traced per-draw rate is unchanged (39.7 versus 41.6 and 40.7 draws/s), and the resident hint is not byte-identical at the rest pose. A software-compositor cost does not justify an art or layer change on this evidence.
spike_will_change.release_window: one browser/server pair on 4051/9251, target closed and server killed in the runner's trap
spike_will_change.control_caveat: The no-transform control is not stable across sessions. First milestone (frozen baseline): 0 of 90 second-frames in all three reps. Spike session (repaired build): 37/0/18/0 of about 90. Re-checked with an arm-identity assertion that proves the swallow hook is installed (own descriptor on torus.style): 15 of 122 and 11 of 125, against shipped 40 of 81 and 43 of 87. So suppressing the per-frame transform write gives a large reduction (about 50% to about 10% of frames over 25 ms) but not elimination, on a faster frame count. The honest claim is 'dominant contributing factor in these sessions', not 'the sole cost', and the absolute second-frame counts are session-dependent. The spike verdict does not depend on this arm: shipped and the three hint arms were measured under one procedure in one session.

network_4g.question: does the cold-localhost LCP survive a modelled 1.5 Mbps phone pipe
network_4g.served_encoding_note: the probe server sends identity encoding, so 31474 bytes of HTML and 6239/4941 bytes of module JS are uncompressed on the wire. This is a pessimistic bound, not the deploy server's brotli/gzip behaviour.
network_4g.device: phone 390x844 dpr3, 4x CPU throttle, cache disabled, service worker bypassed
network_4g.note: about 1.7 s of the 2.7 s is bytes arriving and about 1 s follows arrival. Roughly half of the modelled LCP would move with fewer bytes; the other half would not. This is a modelled bound, not a field or production LCP claim.

corrections: Earlier wording in this file said no-transform reached 0 of 90 second-frames. That was one session and does not reproduce; see spike_will_change.control_caveat.

Second-frame counts are not comparable across sessions with different draw rates: a session that draws at 55/s samples more frames in the same 2.2 s window than one that draws at 36/s. Compare fractions within a session, never raw counts across sessions.

decomposition.question: candidate 1: is the overture cost drawing, canvas area, or compositing

build.note: frozen baseline, not the repaired build, so this decomposition is comparable with the first milestone

decomposition.device: desktop 1440x900 dpr1, 3 reps, ABBA order, cache disabled

arms.draw-1: arcs.mjs replaced: same clearRect cadence, one stroke instead of eight
arms.draw-detached: authored eight-arc stroke work, executed into a detached canvas; visible canvas never invalidated
arms.canvas-hidden: clock, drawing and canvas calls kept, [data-stage-arcs]{visibility:hidden}
arms.canvas-half: probe substitution of the dpr line in stage.mjs: backing store halved in each axis, quarter the pixels
arms.no-mask: authored mask removed on the arcs container
arms.no-transform: torus transform writes suppressed after load

readings: Drawing is not the cost: canvas-hidden still executes the eight-arc draw at ~60/s and shows 0 of 138, 0 of 137 and 0 of 136 frames over 25 ms in three reps.

Canvas invalidation is not the cost either: draw-detached keeps the full stroke work but never touches the visible canvas, and the second-frame fraction stays at shipped levels (0.38/0.42/0.43 against 0.40/0.54/0.68).
Canvas area is a small contributor: quartering the backing store moves the median fraction from 0.54 to 0.37, well short of removing it.

The mask and the per-frame transform each remove part of the cost (no-mask median 0.35, no-transform 0.11 with high variance), so this is a scene-composite interaction rather than one dominant factor: the masked, semi-transparent canvas surface is expensive to composite whenever the frame is being recomposited, and the transform write is what forces that recomposition.

Consequence for the candidate list: there is no faithful single-factor subtraction that removes the cost. Hiding the canvas or dropping the mask or freezing the transform each buys time by removing authored richness, which the acceptance gates forbid. This is a retain, not a repair.
